entries.name: DT-2
entries.text: DT-2 of the donttrade test. Each checked habit now gets one of three results: No sign, Some sign or Clear sign, with a number for how often chance alone gives that result. Re-entering soon after a loss and trading after a losing run are checked in their harmful direction only. A habit needs at least 5 trades in both groups it compares (was 30). The three habits are checked together, with size after a loss shown as facts until its check ships: the steps are cut so that, on histories with no real habit, a Clear sign on any habit turns up at most 5 in 100 times across a first report and its re-test together, and Some sign or Clear sign at most 20 in 100 times in one report. The 'more trades' estimate now comes from your own file: we reshuffle your results so no habit is left, add a habit of a fixed size, and count how often this check catches it. A report or a re-test runs on the method live on the day it runs.

First version of the habit report. It tests up to two habits against chance: re-entering soon after a loss, and trading after a losing run. It describes the hold gap, size after a loss and unusually large losses, with the dollar totals of the matching trades, without testing them. Rows in your file that share a symbol, a direction and an open minute (for example, a position closed in parts) count as one trade. Rows that open at exactly 00:00 and are held a whole number of days, as in exports with dates but no times, are never combined; if they are 5% or more of a file's rows, nothing in that file is tested and size after a loss is not described.
